images.title: Equal opposite sides mean parallel sides
images.purpose: Shows a quadrilateral whose opposite sides are equal, 6 cm and 4 cm, which is a parallelogram with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large parallelogram in the centre with tick marks for equal sides and arrowheads for parallel sides.
images.exact_structure: One parallelogram in dark outline, leaning right, with the long sides top and bottom. The top and bottom sides are thick teal (#0072B2) lines, each carrying one short tick mark and one small arrowhead; the label 6 cm sits under the bottom side and 6 cm above the top side. The two slanting sides are thick amber (#E69F00) lines, each carrying two short tick marks and two small arrowheads; the label 4 cm sits beside each slanting side. No diagonal, no angle marks and no corner letters. Under the shape, centred, the line opposite sides equal. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A quadrilateral whose opposite sides are equal is always a parallelogram.
images.description: Shows a quadrilateral whose opposite sides are equal, 6 cm and 4 cm, which is a parallelogram with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
images.context: Diagonal gives two triangles congruent by SSS, so alternate angles are equal and opposite sides parallel.

image_decisions.why: The lab's tick marks and arrowheads together show the result of this practice in its simplest state.
